title: MFC: Mixed Federated Clustering based on Cross-modal Feature Decoupling

problem.claim: The task is to uncover clustering patterns from heterogeneous, diverse, and unrelated modalities distributed across distinct clients.

gap.claim: Existing federated clustering methods typically assume homogeneous client modalities or different modalities describing the same object, leaving the diverse and unrelated-modality scenario insufficiently addressed.

contributions.claim: A mixed federated clustering model based on cross-modal feature decoupling is proposed.

A client-side decoupling module separates modality-agnostic and modality-specific features through distinct encoders, transmitting only modality-agnostic encoder parameters and clustering centers to the server.
A global consistent complementary clustering module integrates clustering centers from different clients and dispatches global centers back to guide and calibrate local models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present the cross-modal feature decoupling-based mixed federated clustering model as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the server can aggregate modality-agnostic encoders to discover a global clustering structure while avoiding interference from modality-specific noise.
Experiments on three public datasets are reported to show superiority over classic federated clustering methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior methods assume homogeneous modalities or modalities describing the same object, whereas diverse unrelated modalities across clients create an important clustering challenge.
The paper proposes mixed federated clustering based on cross-modal feature decoupling and separates modality-agnostic from modality-specific client features.
The server aggregates modality-agnostic encoders and uses a complementary clustering module to integrate clustering centers across clients.
Global clustering centers are returned to clients to guide and calibrate local clustering models.
Results on three public datasets are reported as superior to classic federated clustering methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the encoders, clustering algorithm, training procedure, communication cost, or privacy properties.
The abstract does not provide ablations or independent verification of the reported superiority.
